To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the use of the 1,2‐dihydro‐3,6‐dihydroxy‐9H‐pyrrolo[3,4‐b]indole (DHI) scaffold in the design of antibacterial agents has led to the discovery of a new class of antibacterial agents, the pyrrolopyridines, that exhibit potent activity against Gram‐positive pathogens, including MRSA, VRSA, VISA, and VRSA.
the basic techniques used in clinical microbiology are important in the development of antibacterials.

(1) the use of the standard method of measuring the MIC for antibacterial agents is inadequate, (2) the use of kill kinetics and the time kill curve method of measuring the antibacterial activity of antibacterial agents is a better method of measuring the activity of antibacterial agent, and (3) the use of time kill curve method to measure the activity of antibacterials is a better method for the measurement of antibacterial agents.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the discovery of novel antibacterial agents.
the discovery, design and evaluation of new antimicrobial agents.
the development of novel antimicrobials and the evaluation of their efficacy in vitro and in vivo.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the basic microbiological techniques are very important and useful in the discovery of antibacterial drugs.
the basic microbiological techniques used in antibiotic discovery are the minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC), minimum bactericidal concentration (MBC), and time kill curves.
the antibacterial activity of a new drug candidate is a function of the MIC, cidal‐ versus static activity, and the possibility of synergy with other antibacterial drugs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of basic clinical microbiology techniques for in vitro assessment of activity of antibacterial agents is a crucial component in the drug discovery process.
the basic clinical microbiology techniques are crucial to the development and development of antibacterial brokers.

the use of the above mentioned techniques in the evaluation of the activity of the antibacterial agents is very important in order to determine the most active agent and the most active combination of the tested compounds.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the development of new antibacterials is a slow, expensive, and uncertain process, with a high risk of failure.
the basic microbiology techniques we used to study the effect of the drug in vitro can be used to study the effects of the drug on other organisms as well.
the development of new antimicrobials requires an integrated, multidisciplinary approach, and the development of new antibacterial drugs is a long, expensive process.
